messages:
Priyanka Bose: For the FP8/INT8 sprint: we need to lock “sanity check” drift thresholds that we can defend + use for gating. What’s acceptable drift for hosted models (chat/completions)?

Priyanka Bose: Specifically: do we gate on (a) numeric drift on logits / per-token logprobs vs FP16 baseline, (b) string output diffs, or (c) task-based eval deltas? We need something that can run fast in CI/perf-canary.

Arjun Desai: +1. For INT8 we’ve seen cases where output is identical for most prompts but a small subset flips a token early (sampling amplification). If we gate on text equality, it’s too strict.

Jonas Weber: Agree text equality is basically a non-starter unless we force greedy + deterministic everywhere.

Jonas Weber: For “fast guardrail”, I’d propose two layers:
1) deterministic mode (temp=0, top_p=1, top_k=0 / disabled) on a small prompt set; compare token-level outputs + logprobs.
2) small “quality smoke” (temp=0.7, realistic params) where we don’t require exact match, but we check aggregated metrics don’t shift beyond a threshold.

Noah Patel: What are we optimizing for? Correctness (no crazy divergence) + no measurable quality regression. For quant, numeric drift is expected; we just need it bounded and consistent.

Grace Kim: Kernel side: we can give you per-op max abs error but that’s not super meaningful at model output level. CI needs something stable across GPUs too.

Claire Dubois: Re: stability: avoid any metric that is very sensitive to nondeterminism (esp. if we’re on shared perf lab). Logit-level comparisons can be stable if we fix seeds + deterministic kernels, but that’s not always true for attention implementations.

Priyanka Bose: We can run deterministic settings in a dedicated CI lane (single GPU type) and keep perf-canary more relaxed. But we need an “acceptable” threshold number.

Arjun Desai: Proposal from quant profiles POV:
- INT8: tighter than FP8 because we expect INT8 calibration to be consistent; but we also have more fallback behavior.
- FP8: allow slightly higher numeric drift but require no “patterned” failures (e.g., long-context prompts exploding).

Isabella Rossi: For the sprint report, we also want to say “no quality regressions observed” in a way that doesn’t overpromise.

Jonas Weber: Here’s what we’ve used elsewhere (rough starting point):
- Logprob drift: median |Δlogp| < 1e-2 and p99 |Δlogp| < 5e-2 over all generated tokens in deterministic mode.
- Top-1 agreement: >= 99.5% of tokens match greedy baseline over the prompt set.
- “Early divergence” rate: < 1% of prompts diverge within first 32 generated tokens.

Jonas Weber: Caveat: the moment a token flips, the rest of the sequence diverges and the token-match metric looks terrible. That’s why “diverge within first N tokens” is a better summary than overall token match.

Noah Patel: +1 “early divergence” metric. Also we should explicitly separate prefill vs decode sensitivity: long-context prefill errors show up as weird TTFT/latency and can also change attention numerics.

Grace Kim: For FP8 long-context: the issues we’ve seen are alignment/stride bugs, not “acceptable drift”. If we hit those, the drift metrics will be huge. So the drift guardrail will catch that.

Priyanka Bose: If we do logprob drift, do we compare raw logits or logprobs after softmax? Raw logits can differ by constant offsets.

Claire Dubois: Compare logprobs for the selected token (or KL between distributions) rather than raw logits. Constant shifts cancel.

Arjun Desai: KL is expensive if we do full vocab, but we can do top-k KL approximation (k=50) or just check top-1/top-5 set overlap.

Jonas Weber: Yeah, full-vocab KL is a no-go in CI. Top-k overlap is cheap-ish and surprisingly informative.

Jonas Weber: Concrete suggestion for CI guardrail (fast, deterministic):
- Run temp=0 greedy for 50 prompts per model family (mix short + long context).
- Metrics:
  a) prompts diverging within first 32 output tokens <= 1/50 (2%)
  b) for non-diverged prompts: median |Δlogp(selected)| <= 0.01, p99 <= 0.05
  c) top-5 overlap rate >= 98% on the first 32 tokens (computed even if top-1 differs)

Noah Patel: Those numbers seem reasonable. But do we need different thresholds for FP8 vs INT8? INT8 should likely be stricter on top-1 / early divergence.

Arjun Desai: I’d set:
- INT8: early divergence <= 1% (so 0/50 ideally), top-5 overlap >= 99%, p99 |Δlogp| <= 0.03
- FP8: early divergence <= 2%, top-5 overlap >= 98%, p99 |Δlogp| <= 0.05

Grace Kim: That aligns with what kernel folks can realistically hit without spending the whole sprint chasing tiny diffs.

Isabella Rossi: For “hosted models” do we apply the same for all families? Qwen sometimes shows more sensitivity in long context.

Priyanka Bose: Maybe thresholds per model family in v1 is overkill. But we can allowlist specific model+GPU combos if needed (with an issue filed).

Claire Dubois: Important: guardrail prompt set must include:
- 1-2 long-context prompts (8k/16k) with structured content
- 1 “mathy” prompt (sensitivity to small changes)
- 1 code completion prompt
- 1 multi-turn chat prompt (system + user)

Priyanka Bose: I can curate a 50-prompt set per family (Llama, Qwen, Mistral) with those categories. Keep it small enough to run nightly.

Jonas Weber: For the non-deterministic “quality smoke” (slower, but still lightweight):
- sample 200 prompts total (not per model) with realistic decoding
- compute embedding-similarity between FP16 and quant outputs (cosine on Redwood embeddings) and require mean cos >= 0.98 and p5 >= 0.95
- plus a few rubric checks (refusal consistency, JSON validity for structured prompts)

Noah Patel: Embedding sim is good for “semantic drift”, but careful: can hide factual regressions. Still OK as smoke.

Arjun Desai: We should also explicitly say: we do not claim equivalence, we claim “no material regression on our sanity suite”.

Priyanka Bose: OK. I’ll write this up as proposed thresholds and ask Connor/Sahana if CI can run greedy + logprob collection.

Grace Kim: If you need per-token logprobs from runtime, ping Yuki or me; there’s already plumbing behind a flag.

Isabella Rossi: :thumbsup: Also, can we log which quant profile was used (FP8 e4m3 vs e5m2) so we can interpret drift?

Arjun Desai: Yes, please. Profile ID + calibration stats should be in the metadata tags.

Jonas Weber: Action items:
- Priyanka: draft thresholds + prompt categories
- Jonas: provide small script to compute early divergence + top-5 overlap + logprob drift
- Arjun: propose INT8 vs FP8 threshold split + allowlist format

Priyanka Bose: Done. I’ll drop a link in-thread once the doc is in the shared drive.

(Claire Dubois added a reaction :eyes:)

Priyanka Bose: Link: https://drive.google.com/…/quant-sanity-evals-notes (WIP). Please comment if the thresholds feel too strict/loose for hosted.

Noah Patel: Skimmed. Looks good. Only tweak: in addition to “diverge within first 32”, also track “diverge at all” so we notice slow drift (rare but happens).

Jonas Weber: +1. “diverge at all” is a useful chart but not a gate.

Priyanka Bose: Updated. Gate = early divergence + logprob drift + top-5 overlap. “Diverge at all” tracked only.

Grace Kim: Great. This should catch the scary stuff (like the FP8 long-context bug) without blocking on harmless differences.

Arjun Desai: :shipit: I’ll sync with Sahana on allowlist format (model+GPU+runtime commit) so we don’t accumulate permanent exceptions.
